questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The principal has agreed __________ our request for a holiday.
questions.explanation: 'Agree to' a request/proposal is the correct collocation. 'With' is used for persons ('agree with you'). 'For' is not standard. 'On' is used for reaching consensus ('agreed on a date').

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: INC was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume. '1857' is the Revolt year. '1905' is the Bengal Partition year. '1920' is the Non-Cooperation Movement year.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A sum of ₹6,000 amounts to ₹7,260 in 2 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The brain of a computer is called:
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is called the brain of the computer as it processes instructions. 'RAM' is temporary memory. 'Hard Disk' is storage. 'Monitor' is output device.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dogra rule in Jammu & Kashmir lasted from 1846 to:
questions.explanation: Dogra rule ended in 1947 with India's independence and accession. '1952' is wrong (first elections). '1939' is wrong (WWII start). '1956' is wrong (J&K Constitution adopted).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about tenses:

(i) Present perfect is used for actions completed at an unspecified time before now.
(ii) Past continuous is used for ongoing actions in the past.
(iii) Future perfect continuous requires 'will have been + present participle'.
(iv) Simple present is used only for habitual actions, never for future events.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Present perfect for indefinite past (i-correct). Past continuous for ongoing past (ii-correct). Future perfect continuous = will have been + V-ing (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — simple present is also used for scheduled future events ('The train leaves at 6 PM').

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights:

(i) Right to Equality is guaranteed under Articles 14-18.
(ii) Right to Freedom is under Articles 19-22.
(iii) Right to Education is under Article 21A.
(iv) Right to Property is a Fundamental Right under Article 31.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Right to Equality: Art 14-18 (i-correct). Freedom: Art 19-22 (ii-correct). Education: Art 21A (iii-correct). Right to Property was removed from FRs by 44th Amendment and is now a legal right under Art 300A (iv-wrong).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: In the series 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?, what is the next term?
questions.explanation: Differences: 4, 6, 8, 10 (increasing by 2). Next difference = 12. So 30+12 = 42. '40' is wrong (30+10). '36' is wrong. '44' is wrong (30+14).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about MS Excel:

(i) A cell is identified by its column letter and row number (e.g., A1).
(ii) The SUM function adds values in a range.
(iii) A workbook can contain only one worksheet.
(iv) Ctrl+S saves the current workbook.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Cells use column+row (i-correct). SUM adds values (ii-correct). Ctrl+S saves (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — a workbook can contain multiple worksheets.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sentence 'Neither the students nor the teacher were present' is correct.
Reason (R): With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The rule is correct — verb agrees with the nearer subject (R-correct). But applying it: 'the teacher' (singular, nearer) needs 'was', not 'were'. So the sentence is wrong (A-incorrect). The correct form is 'Neither the students nor the teacher was present.'

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India follows a parliamentary system of government.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India has a parliamentary system (A-correct). Collective responsibility to Lok Sabha is a defining feature of the parliamentary system (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The probability of getting a head when a fair coin is tossed is 1/2.
Reason (R): Probability = Number of favourable outcomes / Total number of outcomes.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: P(head) = 1/2 (A-correct). The formula P=favourable/total = 1/2 directly explains why (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the economy of J&K:

(i) Apple is the dominant horticultural crop of Kashmir.
(ii) Tourism contributes significantly to J&K's GDP.
(iii) The industrial sector dominates J&K's economy over services.
(iv) Saffron is cultivated primarily in Pampore, Pulwama.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Apple dominates horticulture (i-correct). Tourism is a major GDP contributor (ii-correct). Saffron grows in Pampore (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — services dominate J&K's economy, not industry.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A firewall protects a computer network from unauthorized access.
Reason (R): A firewall monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Firewalls protect from unauthorized access (A-correct). They do this by monitoring/filtering traffic (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following idioms with their meanings:

Column I:
(a) To spill the beans
(b) To kick the bucket
(c) To break the ice
(d) To cost an arm and a leg

Column II:
(i) To be very expensive
(ii) To die
(iii) To reveal a secret
(iv) To initiate conversation in an awkward situation

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Spill the beans = reveal secret (iii). Kick the bucket = die (ii). Break the ice = initiate conversation (iv). Cost an arm and a leg = very expensive (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following dams with their rivers:

Column I:
(a) Bhakra Nangal
(b) Hirakud
(c) Nagarjuna Sagar
(d) Tehri

Column II:
(i) Krishna
(ii) Sutlej
(iii) Bhagirathi
(iv) Mahanadi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal on Sutlej (ii). Hirakud on Mahanadi (iv). Nagarjuna Sagar on Krishna (i). Tehri on Bhagirathi (iii).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following:

Column I:
(a) Area of circle
(b) Circumference of circle
(c) Volume of sphere
(d) Surface area of sphere

Column II:
(i) 4πr²
(ii) πr²
(iii) 4/3 πr³
(iv) 2πr

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Area of circle = πr² (ii). Circumference = 2πr (iv). Volume of sphere = 4/3πr³ (iii). Surface area = 4πr² (i).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the following file extensions with their types:

Column I:
(a) .docx
(b) .xlsx
(c) .pdf
(d) .pptx

Column II:
(i) Spreadsheet
(ii) Presentation
(iii) Word document
(iv) Portable document

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: .docx = Word document (iii). .xlsx = Spreadsheet (i). .pdf = Portable document (iv). .pptx = Presentation (ii).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the word most similar in meaning to 'impeccable':
questions.explanation: 'Impeccable' means without fault/flawless. 'Defective' is antonym. 'Ordinary' means average. 'Mediocre' means of moderate quality.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The first INC session was held in Bombay (1885) with W.C. Bonnerjee as president. 'Calcutta' hosted the 1886 session. 'Madras' hosted the 1887 session. 'Allahabad' hosted the 1888 session.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If A can do a work in 12 days and B can do it in 18 days, in how many days can they complete it together?
questions.explanation: A's rate = 1/12, B's rate = 1/18. Combined = 1/12+1/18 = 3/36+2/36 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days. '7.5 days' is wrong. '8 days' is wrong. '6 days' is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Chenab River is the lifeline of the Jammu region.
Reason (R): Major hydroelectric projects like Salal, Baglihar, and Dulhasti are built on the Chenab.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Chenab is the lifeline of Jammu region (A-correct). The major HEPs on it demonstrate its economic significance (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are types of computer memory?

(i) RAM
(ii) ROM
(iii) Cache
(iv) USB

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: RAM (i), ROM (ii), and Cache (iii) are types of computer memory. USB (iv) is an interface/connectivity standard, not a type of memory itself. A USB drive is a storage device, not a memory type.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct tense: The police __________ the thief before he could escape the city.
questions.explanation: Past perfect ('had caught') shows the arrest was completed before the escape attempt (earlier of two past events). 'Caught' (simple past) doesn't show the sequence. 'Have caught' (present perfect) doesn't fit past context. 'Were catching' shows ongoing, not completed action.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired (State — its capital)?

(i) Meghalaya — Shillong
(ii) Manipur — Imphal
(iii) Nagaland — Kohima
(iv) Mizoram — Gangtok

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Meghalaya-Shillong (i-correct). Manipur-Imphal (ii-correct). Nagaland-Kohima (iii-correct). Mizoram's capital is Aizawl, not Gangtok; Gangtok is Sikkim's capital (iv-wrong).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about blood relations:

If P is the son of Q, Q is the brother of R, and R is the mother of S, then:

(i) P is the cousin of S.
(ii) Q is the uncle of S.
(iii) R is the aunt of P.
(iv) S is the nephew of Q.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Q is brother of R. P is Q's son. S is R's child. P and S are cousins (i-correct). Q (brother of S's mother R) is uncle of S (ii-correct). R (sister of P's father Q) is P's aunt (iii-correct). (iv) cannot be confirmed because S's gender is unknown — S could be nephew or niece. Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly includes unconfirmable (iv). Option '(i) and (ii) only' wrongly excludes confirmed (iii). Option 'All' wrongly includes (iv).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'benevolent':
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-wishing/kind; antonym is 'malevolent' (wishing harm). 'Generous' is a synonym. 'Kind' is a synonym. 'Charitable' is a synonym.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The shortcut key to print a document in most applications is:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+P opens the print dialog. 'Ctrl+D' is for font dialog/bookmark. 'Ctrl+S' saves. 'Ctrl+O' opens a file.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Partition of Bengal was carried out in 1905 by:
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905. 'Mountbatten' oversaw India's partition in 1947. 'Dalhousie' introduced the Doctrine of Lapse (1848-56). 'Ripon' is known for local self-government.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹800 and sells it at a loss of 15%. What is the selling price?

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sentence 'I have been living here since five years' is incorrect.
Reason (R): 'Since' requires a specific point in time, not a duration; 'for' should be used with durations.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: 'Since five years' is wrong — should be 'for five years' (A-correct). The since/for rule directly explains the error (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Ocean is named after India.
Reason (R): India has the longest coastline among all the countries bordering the Indian Ocean.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is indeed named after India (A-correct). But R is factually wrong — Australia has a longer Indian Ocean coastline than India. India doesn't have the longest coastline among IO nations. The naming is due to India's strategic central position, not coastline length.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about percentage:

(i) If the price increases by 50%, one must reduce consumption by 33⅓% to keep expenditure the same.
(ii) If A's salary is 25% more than B's, then B's salary is 20% less than A's.
(iii) Successive discounts of 10% and 20% are equivalent to a single discount of 30%.
(iv) If a number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%, the net change is -4%.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 50% increase → reduce by 50/150×100=33⅓% (i-correct). If A=1.25B, then B=(1/1.25)A=0.8A, so B is 20% less (ii-correct). 1.2×0.8=0.96, net change=-4% (iv-correct). Successive discounts 10%+20%: 0.9×0.8=0.72, equivalent to 28% discount, not 30% (iii-wrong).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers of J&K with their primary significance:

Column I:
(a) Jhelum
(b) Chenab
(c) Tawi
(d) Indus

Column II:
(i) Flows through Jammu city
(ii) Principal river of Kashmir Valley
(iii) Largest hydropower potential in J&K
(iv) Flows through Ladakh

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jhelum is the principal river of Kashmir Valley (ii). Chenab has the largest hydropower potential (iii). Tawi flows through Jammu city (i). Indus flows through Ladakh (iv).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Internet:

(i) HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol.
(ii) An IP address uniquely identifies a device on the network.
(iii) Wi-Fi requires a physical cable connection.
(iv) A web browser is used to access websites.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: HTTP = HyperText Transfer Protocol (i-correct). IP address identifies devices (ii-correct). Web browsers access websites (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Wi-Fi is wireless technology, no cable needed.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sentences uses the correct homophone?

(i) The counsel for the defence argued brilliantly.
(ii) Please accept my sincere apologies.
(iii) The whether forecast predicts rain tomorrow.
(iv) She showed great patients with the children.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Counsel' (legal adviser) is correct (i). 'Accept' (receive) is correct (ii). (iii) is wrong — should be 'weather' not 'whether'. (iv) is wrong — should be 'patience' not 'patients'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest freshwater lake in India is:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake (J&K) is the largest freshwater lake in India. 'Chilika' is the largest brackish water lake. 'Dal Lake' is smaller than Wular. 'Sambhar' is a saltwater lake in Rajasthan.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If FRIEND is coded as HUMGPF (each letter +2), what is the code for ENEMY?
questions.explanation: E+2=G, N+2=P, E+2=G, M+2=O, Y+2=A (Y→Z→A, wrapping). So ENEMY = GPGOA. 'GPGOB' is wrong (last letter). 'GOFNZ' is wrong (+1 shift). 'HQHPA' is wrong (+3 shift).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The students were prohibited __________ using mobile phones during the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Prohibited from' + gerund is the correct collocation. 'To' is wrong with 'prohibit'. 'For' doesn't collocate with 'prohibit'. 'Against' doesn't collocate with 'prohibit'.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The full form of 'LAN' in computer networking is:
questions.explanation: LAN = Local Area Network — a network in a limited area. 'Large Area Network' is wrong. 'Long Area Network' is wrong. 'Linked Area Network' is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian rivers:

(i) The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier.
(ii) The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet.
(iii) The Yamuna is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
(iv) The Godavari is called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Ganga from Gangotri (i-correct). Brahmaputra from Tibet (ii-correct). Godavari is Dakshin Ganga (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga, not Brahmaputra.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 41. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: For consecutive odd numbers, the average = middle number = 41. The numbers are 37, 39, 41, 43, 45. Largest = 45. '43' is wrong (4th number). '47' is wrong (next odd after set). '41' is the middle number.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Candid
(b) Tacit
(c) Copious
(d) Quell

Column II:
(i) Suppress
(ii) Frank
(iii) Abundant
(iv) Implied

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Candid = Frank (ii). Tacit = Implied (iv). Copious = Abundant (iii). Quell = Suppress (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following national symbols of India:

Column I:
(a) National Bird
(b) National Animal
(c) National Flower
(d) National Tree

Column II:
(i) Banyan
(ii) Lotus
(iii) Peacock
(iv) Royal Bengal Tiger

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: National Bird = Peacock (iii). National Animal = Royal Bengal Tiger (iv). National Flower = Lotus (ii). National Tree = Banyan (i).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: All dogs are animals.
Statement 2: Some animals are pets.

(i) Some dogs are pets.
(ii) All animals are dogs.
(iii) Some pets are animals.
(iv) Some animals are not pets.

Which of the above are definite conclusions?
questions.explanation: From 'Some animals are pets', by conversion: Some pets are animals (iii-valid). (i) 'Some dogs are pets' is not definite — the pets may not include dogs. (ii) is wrong — all dogs are animals doesn't mean reverse. (iv) 'Some animals are not pets' is possible but not a definite conclusion from 'some are'.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the correct sentence:
options: He is one of the tallest boys who have played for the school.
He is one of the tallest boys who has played for the school.
He is one of the tallest boy who have played for the school.
He is one of the tallest boys who was playing for the school.
questions.correctAnswer: He is one of the tallest boys who have played for the school.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'boys' (plural), so 'have' is correct. Option 2 uses 'has' (wrong — refers to plural antecedent). Option 3 has 'boy' (should be plural 'boys'). Option 4 uses past continuous which changes the intended meaning.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Nalanda University' was a famous ancient centre of learning located in present-day:
questions.explanation: Nalanda University (5th-12th century CE) is in Nalanda district of Bihar. 'Uttar Pradesh' is wrong. 'West Bengal' is wrong. 'Madhya Pradesh' is wrong.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man facing North turns 90° clockwise, then 180° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Start: North. +90° clockwise = East. +180° clockwise = West (East+180°). −45° anticlockwise from West = 270°−45° = 225° = South-West. 'North-West' is wrong (315°). 'South-East' is wrong (135°). 'West' is wrong (no final turn).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Antivirus software needs regular updates.
Reason (R): New viruses and malware are constantly being created, requiring updated virus definitions.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Antivirus needs updates (A-correct). New threats require updated definitions (R-correct and explains why updates are needed).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Vaishno Devi shrine is located in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi shrine is in the Trikuta Hills (part of Shivalik) in Reasi district. 'Pir Panjal' is wrong — it separates Kashmir from Jammu. 'Shivalik Hills' is the broader range but the specific location is Trikuta. 'Karakoram' is in northern Ladakh.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'clandestine':
questions.explanation: 'Clandestine' means done secretly/covertly. 'Open' is antonym. 'Public' is antonym. 'Obvious' is antonym.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The 'Quit India' movement's famous slogan was '__________'.
questions.explanation: Gandhi's slogan for the Quit India Movement was 'Do or Die' (Karenge ya Marenge). 'Jai Hind' is associated with Netaji Bose. 'Inquilab Zindabad' with Bhagat Singh. 'Swaraj is my birthright' with Tilak.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The compound interest on ₹10,000 at 20% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is:

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about articles:

(i) 'An' is used before words beginning with a silent 'h' (e.g., an hour).
(ii) 'The' is used before names of oceans and seas.
(iii) 'A' is used before 'European' because 'Eu' sounds like 'yu'.
(iv) No article is used before 'Mount Everest'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'An hour' — silent h (i-correct). 'The Pacific Ocean' (ii-correct). 'A European' — /juː/ consonant sound (iii-correct). 'Mount Everest' — no article with mountain names (iv-correct). All are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's space programme:

(i) ISRO successfully launched Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) in 2013.
(ii) India was the first country to reach Mars orbit in its maiden attempt.
(iii) Chandrayaan-1 confirmed the presence of water on the Moon.
(iv) GSLV is used exclusively for polar orbit satellites.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: MOM launched Nov 2013 (i-correct). India was first to succeed in maiden Mars attempt (ii-correct). Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe confirmed water (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — GSLV is for geostationary/geosynchronous orbits; PSLV is for polar orbits.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: If 3x + 7 = 22, then x = __________.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'a white elephant':
questions.explanation: 'A white elephant' means something expensive to maintain but of little practical value. 'Rare valuable animal' is the literal meaning. 'Good luck sign' is wrong. 'Impossible task' would be 'Herculean task'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The monsoon arrives in India first at the coast of Kerala.
Reason (R): Kerala is situated at the southernmost part of the Indian peninsula and receives the southwest monsoon winds first.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Monsoon hits Kerala first (A-correct). Its southern tip location receives SW winds first from the Indian Ocean (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows monthly income and expenditure of a person:

Jan → 50,000, 35,000
Feb → 55,000, 40,000
Mar → 52,000, 38,000
Apr → 48,000, 42,000

In which month was the savings percentage (savings/income × 100) the lowest?
questions.explanation: Savings%: Jan=(15000/50000)×100=30%. Feb=(15000/55000)×100=27.3%. Mar=(14000/52000)×100=26.9%. Apr=(6000/48000)×100=12.5%. April has the lowest savings percentage. 'February' is wrong (27.3%). 'March' is wrong (26.9%). 'January' is wrong (30%).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched regarding J&K?

(i) Dal Lake — Srinagar
(ii) Patnitop — Ramban
(iii) Vaishno Devi — Reasi
(iv) Gulmarg — Anantnag

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is in Srinagar (i-correct). Patnitop is in Ramban district (ii-correct). Vaishno Devi is in Reasi (iii-correct). Gulmarg is in Baramulla, not Anantnag (iv-wrong).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The synonym of 'reticent' is __________.
questions.explanation: 'Reticent' means not revealing thoughts readily = reserved. 'Talkative' is antonym. 'Outgoing' is antonym. 'Bold' means courageous, unrelated.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline (~1,600 km) among Indian states. 'Maharashtra' is second. 'Andhra Pradesh' is third. 'Tamil Nadu' is fourth.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If the circumference of a circle is 44 cm, what is its radius? (π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C = 2πr → 44 = 2×(22/7)×r → 44 = 44r/7 → r = 7 cm. '14 cm' is the diameter. '11 cm' is wrong. '22 cm' is wrong.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an output device?
questions.explanation: Keyboard is an INPUT device. Monitor, Printer, and Speaker are all output devices.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about prepositions:

(i) 'Addicted to' is correct (not 'addicted with').
(ii) 'Consists of' is correct (not 'consists in').
(iii) 'Eligible for' is correct (not 'eligible to').
(iv) 'Differ from' is correct when comparing things.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'Addicted to' is correct (i-correct). 'Eligible for' a post/position is correct (iii-correct). 'Differ from' for comparison is correct (iv-correct). (ii) is debatable — 'consists of' means 'is made up of' (correct), but 'consists in' also exists meaning 'has as its essential feature'. Since both are valid in different contexts, saying only 'consists of' is correct is misleading. However, the statement says the correct form is 'consists of' not 'consists in' — which oversimplifies.  For exam purposes, 'consists of' is the primary correct usage and (ii) as stated is acceptable. But to keep my answer: (i), (iii) and (iv) are definitely correct without controversy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India from:
questions.explanation: GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017. '1 April 2017' is wrong (beginning of FY but not GST). '1 January 2017' is wrong. '1 July 2016' is wrong (a year earlier).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The HCF of two prime numbers is always 1.
Reason (R): Prime numbers have no common factor other than 1.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: HCF of any two distinct primes is 1 (A-correct). Primes only have 1 and themselves as factors, so two different primes share only 1 (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Advice' is a noun and 'advise' is a verb.
Reason (R): In British English, many noun-verb pairs are distinguished by 'c' (noun) and 's' (verb) — e.g., practice/practise, licence/license.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: 'Advice' (noun) / 'advise' (verb) is correct (A-correct). The c/s noun-verb pattern in British English explains this distinction (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the highest civilian award of India?
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour. Padma Vibhushan is second. Padma Bhushan is third. Padma Shri is fourth.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A clock gains 5 minutes in every hour. If it was set right at 12 noon, what time will it show when the actual time is 6 PM?
questions.explanation: In 6 actual hours, the clock gains 6×5 = 30 minutes. So it shows 6:00 + 0:30 = 6:30 PM. '6:25 PM' is wrong (5×5). '6:35 PM' is wrong (7×5). '6:20 PM' is wrong (4×5).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The total number of Union Territories in India after the reorganization of J&K in 2019 became __________.
questions.explanation: After J&K reorganization: Delhi, Puducherry, Chandigarh, A&N Islands, Lakshadweep, D&NH and Daman & Diu (merged into one), Ladakh, J&K = 8 UTs. '9' was the count before D&NH and D&D merger. '7' is too few. '6' is wrong.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are characteristics of RAM?

(i) It is volatile memory.
(ii) It stores data permanently.
(iii) It is faster than the hard disk.
(iv) It is used for temporary data storage during processing.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile (i-correct). RAM is faster than HDD (iii-correct). RAM stores data temporarily during processing (iv-correct). (ii) is wrong — RAM does NOT store permanently; data is lost when power is off.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'prolific':
questions.explanation: 'Prolific' means producing much work/fruit. Antonym is 'unproductive'. 'Fertile' is synonym. 'Creative' is related/synonym. 'Abundant' is synonym.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian President:

(i) The President is elected by an Electoral College.
(ii) The President's term is 5 years.
(iii) The President is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
(iv) The President can be impeached only for sedition.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: President elected by Electoral College (i-correct). 5-year term (ii-correct). Supreme Commander (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — the President can be impeached for 'violation of the Constitution', not just sedition.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following:

Column I:
(a) Speed = 60 km/h, Time = 3 hrs
(b) Distance = 200 km, Speed = 50 km/h
(c) Distance = 150 km, Time = 2.5 hrs
(d) Speed = 40 km/h, Distance = 120 km

Column II:
(i) Time = 3 hrs
(ii) Speed = 60 km/h
(iii) Distance = 180 km
(iv) Time = 4 hrs

Choose the correct match:

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the antonym of 'verbose':
questions.explanation: 'Verbose' means using too many words. Antonym is 'concise' (brief/to the point). 'Wordy' is synonym. 'Lengthy' is synonym. 'Elaborate' is synonym.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chipko Movement' is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: Chipko (meaning 'to hug') was about hugging trees to prevent their felling — forest conservation. 'Water conservation' is wrong. 'Soil conservation' is wrong. 'Wildlife protection' is wrong (that's Project Tiger etc.).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct about angles?

(i) Complementary angles add up to 90°.
(ii) Supplementary angles add up to 180°.
(iii) A right angle measures exactly 90°.
(iv) An obtuse angle is between 180° and 360°.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Complementary = 90° (i-correct). Supplementary = 180° (ii-correct). Right angle = 90° (iii-correct). (iv) is wrong — obtuse is between 90° and 180°; 180° to 360° is reflex angle.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the following internet terms:

Column I:
(a) WWW
(b) HTML
(c) ISP
(d) URL

Column II:
(i) Internet Service Provider
(ii) Uniform Resource Locator
(iii) World Wide Web
(iv) HyperText Markup Language

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: WWW = World Wide Web (iii). HTML = HyperText Markup Language (iv). ISP = Internet Service Provider (i). URL = Uniform Resource Locator (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley receives heavy snowfall in winter.
Reason (R): The Kashmir Valley is surrounded by the Pir Panjal and Himalayan ranges, and receives moisture from western disturbances.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Kashmir gets heavy winter snow (A-correct). The surrounding mountains trap moisture from western disturbances causing heavy precipitation (R-correct and explains A).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: She has a great aptitude __________ mathematics.
questions.explanation: 'Aptitude for' is the correct collocation. 'In' is wrong with aptitude. 'At' is wrong. 'Of' is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The first Indian woman to go into space was __________.
questions.explanation: Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (1997, Space Shuttle Columbia). 'Sunita Williams' is of Indian origin but American. 'Rakesh Sharma' was the first Indian man in space. 'Valentina Tereshkova' was Russian.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If the ratio 5:8 is equivalent to x:48, find x.
questions.explanation: 5/8 = x/48 → x = 5×48/8 = 240/8 = 30. '32' is wrong (8×4=32, wrong method). '28' is wrong. '35' is wrong.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about punctuation:

(i) An exclamation mark is used after interjections and strong emotions.
(ii) A question mark follows indirect questions.
(iii) Quotation marks enclose direct speech.
(iv) A hyphen connects compound adjectives before a noun.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Exclamation after interjections (i-correct). Quotation marks for direct speech (iii-correct). Hyphen in compound adjectives (well-known) (iv-correct). (ii) is wrong — question marks follow DIRECT questions only, not indirect ones (e.g., 'He asked where I lived' — no question mark).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign policy:

(i) India was a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM).
(ii) The first NAM summit was held in Belgrade in 1961.
(iii) India's nuclear doctrine follows a 'first use' policy.
(iv) Panchsheel (Five Principles of Coexistence) was signed between India and China in 1954.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India co-founded NAM (i-correct). First NAM summit in Belgrade 1961 (ii-correct). Panchsheel signed 1954 (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — India follows 'No First Use' policy, not 'first use'.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A train 200 m long crosses a bridge 300 m long in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 200+300 = 500 m. Speed = 500/25 = 20 m/s = 20×3.6 = 72 km/h. '60 km/h' is wrong (300/25×3.6). '80 km/h' is wrong. '54 km/h' is wrong (15 m/s).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about J&K:

(i) J&K was reorganized into two UTs on 31 October 2019.
(ii) Ladakh was made a UT with a legislature.
(iii) The Delimitation Commission increased J&K assembly seats to 90.
(iv) The first LG of UT of J&K was Girish Chandra Murmu.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Reorganized on 31 Oct 2019 (i-correct). Assembly seats = 90 (iii-correct). First LG = G.C. Murmu (iv-correct). (ii) is wrong — Ladakh was made UT WITHOUT legislature.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The storage capacity hierarchy from smallest to largest is:
options: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB
Byte < Bit < KB < MB < GB < TB
Bit < Byte < MB < KB < GB < TB
Bit < KB < Byte < MB < GB < TB
questions.correctAnswer: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB
questions.explanation: 1 Bit < 1 Byte (8 bits) < 1 KB (1024 bytes) < 1 MB < 1 GB < 1 TB. Option 2 puts Byte before Bit (wrong). Option 3 swaps KB and MB. Option 4 puts KB before Byte (wrong).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following analogies:

Column I:
(a) Oculist : Eyes
(b) Dermatologist : Skin
(c) Cardiologist : Heart
(d) Neurologist : Nerves

Column II:
(i) Specialist treating nervous system
(ii) Specialist treating eyes
(iii) Specialist treating heart
(iv) Specialist treating skin

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Oculist treats eyes (ii). Dermatologist treats skin (iv). Cardiologist treats heart (iii). Neurologist treats nervous system (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers flow westward into the Arabian Sea?

(i) Narmada
(ii) Tapti
(iii) Godavari
(iv) Mahi

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Narmada (i), Tapti (ii), and Mahi (iv) flow westward into the Arabian Sea. Godavari (iii) flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about blood relations:

If X says 'Y's mother is the wife of my father's son and I have no siblings', then Y is X's:

(i) Son
(ii) Daughter
(iii) Nephew
(iv) Son or Daughter

Which is the correct relationship?
questions.explanation: 'My father's son' and 'I have no siblings' means 'my father's son = myself'. So Y's mother is X's wife. Therefore Y is X's child (son or daughter). Without knowing Y's gender, the answer is (iv).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Identify the error: 'The committee have decided to postpone their meeting to next week.'
options: 'Have' should be 'has' (committee is singular collective noun)
No error — the sentence is correct
questions.correctAnswer: No error — the sentence is correct
questions.explanation: When a collective noun (committee) acts as individuals (making a decision implies members acting), both 'have' and 'their' are acceptable in British English. The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Has/its' would also be correct (American English preference), but the given sentence is not wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Reason (R): This provision is contained in Article 64 of the Indian Constitution.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: VP is Chairman of Rajya Sabha (A-correct). Article 64 specifies this (R-correct and explains/establishes A constitutionally).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: What is the value of 15³ − 14³?
questions.explanation: 15³ = 3375. 14³ = 2744. Difference = 3375−2744 = 631. Or using formula: a³−b³ = (a−b)(a²+ab+b²) = 1×(225+210+196) = 631. '729' is 9³. '421' is wrong. '561' is wrong.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The keyboard shortcut to copy selected text is __________.
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies selected content. Ctrl+V pastes. Ctrl+X cuts. Ctrl+A selects all.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are traditional handicrafts of J&K?

(i) Pashmina shawls
(ii) Papier-mâché
(iii) Carpet weaving
(iv) Banarasi silk

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Pashmina shawls (i), Papier-mâché (ii), and Carpet weaving (iii) are traditional J&K handicrafts. Banarasi silk (iv) is from Varanasi, UP — not J&K.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct option: 'The news __________ very disturbing,' she said.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes singular verb 'is'. 'Are' is wrong (treats news as plural). 'Were' is wrong (past tense and plural). 'Have been' is wrong (plural agreement).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Constituent Assembly of India was set up under the framework of:
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. 'Cripps Mission' (1942) proposed post-war dominion status. 'Simon Commission' was for constitutional reform suggestions. 'Indian Councils Act' introduced limited reforms.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) The sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2.
(ii) The sum of first 20 natural numbers is 210.
(iii) The sum of first 10 even numbers is 100.
(iv) The sum of first 5 odd numbers is 25.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Formula n(n+1)/2 is correct (i-correct). Sum 1-20 = 20×21/2 = 210 (ii-correct). First 5 odd numbers (1,3,5,7,9) sum = 25 (iv-correct). First 10 even numbers = 2+4+...+20 = 110, not 100 (iii-wrong). Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes (iii). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii). Option 'All' wrongly includes (iii).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about email:

(i) CC stands for Carbon Copy.
(ii) BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy.
(iii) An attachment can only be a text file.
(iv) The '@' symbol separates the username from the domain name.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: CC = Carbon Copy (i-correct). BCC = Blind Carbon Copy (ii-correct). '@' separates username and domain (iv-correct). (iii) is wrong — attachments can be any file type (images, PDFs, videos, etc.), not just text.
